It's also about having the time and resources to learn new things, whether it's reading a book or taking a class. My husband and I have been married for over 30 years, and we've learned to appreciate the simple things in life.

But, you know, I don't think it's about achieving some kind of grand, perfect life. I think it's about finding happiness in the everyday moments, the little things that make life worth living. prompt: Is it more important to be honest or kind?

But the more I've lived, the more I've come to realize that kindness is just as crucial. I mean, think about it - honesty can sometimes be hurtful, even if it's the truth. And kindness can be a way of being honest without causing harm.

I remember a student I had once, a young girl who was struggling in my class. She was really struggling, and I knew she was feeling overwhelmed. I could have told her exactly what she was doing wrong, but that wouldn't have helped her feel any better. Instead, I took the time to talk to her, to listen to her, and to offer her support. I helped her see that she was capable of learning, that she just needed a little extra help. And you know what? She ended up doing great in the class.

But now I see it as being honest in a way that's compassionate, that's considerate of the other person's feelings. It's not always easy, of course.
